finalText:
Both combine changes from one branch into another, but they leave different history behind.

**Merge** keeps every commit as it happened and adds one new commit that ties the two branches together. Nothing gets rewritten, so it's safe on shared branches, but your history ends up with extra tie-together commits and a less straight-line story.

**Rebase** takes your commits and replays them on top of the other branch, one by one, as if you'd started from there. History stays a straight line with no tie-together commits, but it rewrites your commits into new ones — so never rebase a branch other people are also working on.

Rule of thumb: rebase your own feature branch to keep it clean before sharing it. Merge when bringing finished work into a shared branch like `main`, or any time the branch is already public.
